To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed new methods for designing constrained codes for DNA-based storage that account for maximum repetition length and/or AT/GC balance constraints.

(1) the redundancy of codes which account for maximum repetition length is approximately equal to that of the corresponding unconstrained codes; (2) the redundancy of constrained codes is significantly higher than that of unconstrained codes which account for AT/GC balance; (3) the redundancy of balanced codes which account for both maximum repetition length and balance is significantly higher than the redundancy of the corresponding codes which account for only one of the constraints.
